Compute a cell-type composition matrix from deconvolution subgroups

compute.composition.matrix.Rd

Builds a binary presence matrix indicating which original cell types are present in each cell group. Each feature of a cell group is opened down to its original deconvolution features (a subgroup is replaced by its members), and the cell type of each feature is read from its name with the cell type vocabulary of multideconv (multideconv::get_cell_type_nomenclature()). Cell types are therefore named as in that vocabulary: for example the LM22 features Plasma.cells and T.cells.CD4.memory.activated are counted as Plasma and CD4.memory.activated, as in the names of the deconvolution subgroups.

Usage

compute.composition.matrix(dt, cell_groups, cells_extra = NULL)

Arguments

dt

Deconvolution subgroups as returned by multideconv::compute.deconvolution.analysis() (the elements Deconvolution matrix and Deconvolution subgroups composition are used).

cell_groups

The cell groups returned by construct_cell_groups(): its element Composition (the features of each cell group) is used. An unnamed list whose second element holds the composition is also accepted.

cells_extra

Optional character vector of additional cell type names, added to the vocabulary used to recognise cell types in the feature names.

Value

A binary matrix (data.frame) where rows are cell groups and columns are cell types (1 = present, 0 = absent). Rows are named as the cell groups, as the features of compute.latent_factors(). Cell types not present in any cell group are dropped, and cell groups whose cell types are not recognised (their row is all zeros) are listed, each with a message.

Examples

data("network.tuto")
data("deconv_subgroups.tuto")
cell_groups <- construct_cell_groups(network.tuto, deconv_subgroups.tuto)
